clips.title: The story
paras: Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a water sample. From Moonglade, she asks them to bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it can help explain the poison harming wildlife.

Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, with springs and pools high above the dry northern Barrens. Their waters shape local weather and moisture. The Burning Blade, a cult devoted to demons, has taken hold on the crags. Dendrite Starblaze fears their foul sorcery may taint the basin around this important mountain.

Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and turns to the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. Druids who reach the peak and bring back a sample of its tainted water give Tonga what he needs to study the sickness and brew an antidote.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Dreadmist Peak to the northwest of the Crossroads is most likely a primary candidate as to the source of the spread of the poison. Its airy peaks have pools of water that influence the weather patterns. I suspect the water is now tainted by the demon-worshipping Burning Blade.

Use this sampler to draw water from the pool at the very top of the peak. Once filled, deliver it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads. He is the one that requested our aid, and you will work with him to address this malady.

clips.title: Progress
paras: You are the one that the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade sent, yes? This is most fortuitous for us! We are stymied in our effort to bring balance to the sickly gazelles that wander the northern Barrens; we're happy for all the help we can get.
Do you have the sample of water that Dendrite Starblaze said you'd have? He notified me that you'd draw one so we could work on a cure together...

clips.title: Completion
paras: By my ancestors, this water is disgusting! No wonder the gazelles are sick.

Something is polluting the water, and in turn beginning to wreck the northern Barrens ecosystem. Sick gazelles have been sighted all north of the east-west road here. While this water is most likely a primary source of the sickness spreading, there's something else at work here.
This water, believe it or not, will help us formulate a cure. While I research this water, I have need of some items to formulate a cure...
